_comment: rock_bars: A CAVE WALL WITH SLOTS, not a row of bars (Ryan: "less like carved bars and more like a cave wall with slots through it"). One mass of the map's own hell rock spans the 10.6 x 8.5 m gallery cross-section -- no sill, no lintel, no uprights -- its two faces swelling and thinning on their own (half-thickness 0.115 .. 0.50 m, heaviest at the haunch into the floor and under the brow at the crest, so the wall is 0.23 m through at its thinnest and 1.00 m at its deepest), its last band under the ceiling broken rather than sawn (up to 0.42 m, line by line; the top row itself is dead flat at 8.5 because map_base's gallery ceiling is exactly CEIL_H 8.5 m over the deck and a knocked-out crest would be a letterbox of daylight over the gate). Eight slots are cut clean through it, no two alike: each has its own width, lean, kink, taper and its own head and foot, and the rock left between them is never under ROCK_MIN 0.50 m (below that a column stops being a mass and starts being a bar) with the spare width piled onto two or three real masses by ROCK_SKEW rather than shared out evenly -- 0.41 .. 1.40 m as built, so the screen has no rhythm to read off. Every row of the lattice carries its own x and z wobble, which is what makes a cut edge ragged instead of milled. THE GUARANTEE IS UNCHANGED: no opening exceeds 0.38 m at any height, so a body (0.8 m across) cannot pass and a rifle round and a sight line can -- tools/modelling/rock_bars_check.py measures it off the shipped .glb rather than asserting it. The envelope is unchanged too (10.6 x 8.5 m, origin the base centre, y=0 the ground, slots span local X, thickness along local Z), because forest_bars.glb and marble_bars.glb are drop-ins for it. ONE CONTIGUOUS MESH: the faces, the reveals and the caps all index one lattice of shared vertices, so components 1 and duplicate positions 0 come out of the topology, not out of a weld. TEXTURE: map 1's own rock through lib/texel.py, not an atlas (Ryan: "the texturing on the gate is bad, you seemed to fix it for the maps generally") -- map_base_build.py's rock and shade painters verbatim, the same seeds, the same tx.MPT 0.05 m per texel as map_base's walls, world-projected in the model's own frame ("box"), so marks run across face edges instead of each face carrying its own cut-off window. Two sheets and no more: map_base has a third, `ember`, and five glowing reveal faces did look good in here, but the Ring measures materials=16 on main against test_map_draw_budgets.gd's ceiling of 18, and a third material for ten triangles would spend the map's last slot on a detail the rock sheet's own emissive specks already carry. Two sheets is two surfaces; the scene's 1.30 X scale on the RockBars node puts those texels at 0.065 m across the lane and 0.05 m in height and thickness. RockBarsCollision is one box per rock column (9 of them, floor to ceiling) plus a sill under the lowest slot foot and a lintel over the highest slot head, shipped as a `-colonly` node: the slot lanes are left OPEN, which is what lets a round and a sight line through what a body cannot pass. Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `max_tris` counts only what is drawn.
